sql:
SELECT cls, (fished_date_doy/20)::int*20 AS doy_bucket,
       count(*) AS n_boat_trips,
       sum(yt) AS total_yt,
       sum(anglers) AS total_anglers,
       round(sum(yt)/nullif(sum(anglers),0), 3) AS ypa
FROM trips
WHERE fished_date_season = 6 AND cls IN ('hd_am','hd_pm','hd_unspecified','hd_twilight','three_quarter','day_1_5','overnight','full_day')
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 1,2

# Notes — S06 d121 planning turn

## State: $100 budgtet, 0 PTO left, season score 13.98 (rank 3/34 this season!)
The d60-note directive worked extremely well: nightly-self switched from the
season-2 "wait for autumn" persona default to booking THREE_QUARTER hard
starting d93. Result: 1 OVERNIGHT + 10 THREE_QUARTER bookings between d93-d112,
$1900 spent, season_score 13.9827 (rank 3, just behind frontloader 14.57 and
elnino 14.25). Shares per trip were consistently strong: 0.80-2.34, several
>1.0. This confirms the d60 finding: season 6 has NO dead spring — three_quarter
stayed hot (pooled ypa 1.0-1.8) through every 20-day bucket from doy0 to doy120
(latest data, just queried). day_1_5 was even hotter early (2.2-2.5 ypa doy0-40)
but at $550/trip buys far fewer trips per budget dollar than three_quarter's
$150 — since **season score is a raw SUM of shares, not $-adjusted**, volume of
cheap high-ypa trips (three_quarter) generally beats fewer expensive ones
(day_1_5) for total season score. HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT stayed near-zero
(0.0-0.3 ypa) in every bucket through doy120 — confirmed structurally dead,
not just "early spring."

## THE MISTAKE: PTO ladder committed ahead of budget, wasted 5 PTO days
pto_committed shows 10 dates (d105,106,107,110,111,112,113,114,117,118) but
only 5 of them (105,107,110,111,112) actually got a matching booking. The
other 5 (106,113,114,117,118) were committed 14 days out on a ladder, but by
the time those dates arrived the $2000 budget was already down to ~$100
(exhausted by d112's booking) — so those 5 committed PTO days could never be
converted into a trip. PTO is deducted immediately and never refunded, so
those 5 days are gone for nothing. **Lesson for next time a budget is fresh:
don't pre-commit a long PTO ladder in one go. Commit PTO for a weekday trip
14 days out only if a rough budget projection (current budget minus the cost
of trips already committed/likely to book before that date) will still cover
the fare when that date actually arrives. Re-check before extending the
ladder further, in small batches (2-3 days), not all 10 PTO at once.**

## Current situation (d121, 0 PTO, $100): almost nothing left to do
With 0 PTO, only trips that need **zero PTO** are legal: TWILIGHT (any day,
$80) or HD_AM/HD_PM on a weekend/holiday ($80). THREE_QUARTER ($150),
DAY_1_5 ($550), OVERNIGHT ($400) are all unaffordable now regardless of PTO.
With $100 budget, at most **one** more $80 trip is possible this whole
season (Apr-Nov budget doesn't carry to next season, so there's no reason to
hoard the $100 — spend it on the best positive-EV shot that shows up, don't
wait). BUT: HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT are confirmed near-dead in the class-pooled
data through doy120 (0.0-0.3 ypa every bucket). Don't force a bet on class-
average alone — only take the last $80 shot if a SPECIFIC scheduled boat
shows real recent signal (e.g., >0 yt on last 1-2 trips, not just nonzero
pooled trailing 30d which can hide zeros). Otherwise it's fine to end the
season not spending the last $100 — there is no penalty for leftover budget,
only opportunity cost, and the opportunity here is thin.

## Directive for remaining nightly decisions this season (d121 → ~d330)
1. Do NOT commit any more PTO — you have 0 left and can't anyway.
2. Do NOT attempt to book THREE_QUARTER/DAY_1_5/OVERNIGHT/FULL_DAY — budget
   ($100) is below their fares ($150/$550/$400/likely $275). These will be
   rejected; don't waste turns reasoning about them.
3. Watch TWILIGHT (any day) and weekend/holiday HD_AM/HD_PM ($80, 0 PTO)
   only. Book the best one if a specific boat shows a real recent bite
   (nonzero last-trip yt, ideally 2 boat-trips running). Otherwise pass.
4. After that one trip (or if none ever looks good), there is nothing left
   to decide for the rest of the season — journal briefly and move on each
   night, no need for deep analysis once budget/PTO hit zero for real.

## Lessons for the NEXT planning turn / next season's start
- Re-run this doy-bucket ypa query fresh at every planning turn (season
  start especially) — don't assume "dead spring, wait for autumn" from the
  persona or from season 2 (practice season). Season 6 disproved it outright:
  check the actual current season's data first.
- THREE_QUARTER at $150 is the best trip-count-per-dollar high-ypa class
  seen in 2 seasons now (season 2 real bloom was DAY_1_5-driven and late,
  season 6 was THREE_QUARTER-driven and early/sustained) — always check it
  first, it's cheap enough to buy many trips.
- When budget is fresh ($2000) and a hot class is confirmed, book
  aggressively (this turn's approach was right) but PACE the PTO ladder:
  commit only 2-3 weekday PTO days ahead at a time, check remaining budget
  before committing more. Target: budget and PTO should hit zero at
  roughly the same time, not budget first with PTO stranded.
- Rough math check for next time: $2000 / $150 ≈ 13 three_quarter trips is
  the real ceiling if that class is hot all season — pace bookings (not
  necessarily PTO-days) so that ~13 fills are spread if the hot window looks
  likely to last the whole season, but if evidence only covers a short
  window, front-load like we did here (it worked: rank 3 season, 13.98 score).

## Forum
Not posting this turn — nothing new since last check (forum_new empty), and
with budget/PTO exhausted there's no more edge to protect or benefit from
sharing. Will reconsider at season end / next season start.
